findings.title: Negative offset slicing on Django QuerySet is unsupported and bypasses bounds
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes a negative cursor.offset straight into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django raises AssertionError('Negative indexing is not supported') for negative slice bounds, so a user-supplied cursor like 'value:-5:0' causes a 500. The comments claim the ORM handles this and that it exposes data 'beyond normal pagination bounds', which is wrong. Cursor.from_string accepts negative ints from user input, and no validation rejects them.

findings.title: Change to BasePaginator allows negative offset for prev cursors
findings.body: In the shared BasePaginator, start_offset is now `offset` unclamped when cursor.is_prev. Previously the offset was passed through as is, so this adds nothing, but the comment says it deliberately allows negatives. A user-controlled negative offset in a prev cursor now reaches queryset slicing for every paginator that subclasses BasePaginator, causing an assertion error (500). The original behavior should be kept, with negative offsets rejected explicitly (as OffsetPaginator does with BadPaginationError).

findings.title: Undocumented query flag gates an unvalidated code path; access check is fragile
findings.body: The optimized_pagination=true flag routes to a paginator with unvalidated negative-offset behavior. The gate `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` can raise AttributeError if member is None (e.g. superuser not in the org), causing a 500 for requests even when the flag isn't set, since it's evaluated unconditionally. It also changes the audit log endpoint for all requests.

findings.title: Prev-cursor trimming uses unclamped offset and is duplicated code
findings.body: `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` uses the raw offset, which with negative offsets will never match the actual fetched length, so the extra row is not dropped. Also OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates the whole BasePaginator.get_result, and get_item_key uses math.floor on a datetime (order_by is -datetime), which raises TypeError. The optimized path is broken for the audit log endpoint.

findings.title: No tests added for new paginator or endpoint behavior
findings.body: A new paginator, a new query parameter and a modified base paginator are introduced without any tests, including negative-offset and permission-gated paths.
